selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline state before changes (mounts, fstab, tmp.mount status)
selected_evidence.summary: Showed /dev/shm mounted nosuid,nodev (no noexec) and tmp.mount disabled/inactive prior to changes

selected_evidence.requirement: Configuration applied: fstab entry for /dev/shm and systemd tmp.mount.d override for /tmp, enabled and applied live
selected_evidence.summary: Applied fstab tmpfs /dev/shm line and tmp.mount.d/override.conf, ran daemon-reload, enabled/started tmp.mount, remounted /dev/shm; findmnt confirms rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec on both /tmp and /dev/shm; tmp.mount shown enabled and fstab shows the /dev/shm line

selected_evidence.requirement: Functional proof that program execution and setuid bits are ignored on /tmp and /dev/shm
selected_evidence.summary: Executing a chmod +x script in /tmp and /dev/shm both returned Permission denied (rc=126); a setuid-root file created in /tmp retained the SUID bit in ls/stat output but is unusable since nosuid is enforced by the mount

selected_evidence.requirement: Functional proof that device nodes are ignored (nodev) on /tmp and /dev/shm
selected_evidence.summary: mknod created the special file entries (filesystem-level op, unaffected by nodev) but opening those device nodes for read/write on both /tmp and /dev/shm returned Permission denied, proving the kernel ignores device semantics on nodev mounts

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline boot identity and healthy mount state for node1
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id bf4e9cbb-84f9-45f0-9b81-6602b98cea07 and confirmed /tmp and /dev/shm both mounted rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec with tmp.mount enabled, immediately before the restart
Issued systemd reboot on node1 asynchronously; command stream closed as expected due to the node going down for restart

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proven via changed boot identity, and command execution available again
selected_evidence.summary: Polling first timed out while node1 was down, then succeeded with boot_id d431d1d5-f456-4103-80ec-ec0f6f2f6086 -- different from baseline bf4e9cbb..., proving an actual restart occurred

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: /tmp and /dev/shm hardening persisted and remains functionally enforced
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, findmnt shows /tmp and /dev/shm both tmpfs rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec, tmp.mount is enabled and active, and repeated exec/setuid functional tests again show Permission denied on execution attempts, confirming the hardening survived the restart

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== boot id baseline =="
cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
uptime -s

set -Eeuo pipefail

echo "STEP 1: configure /dev/shm hardening via /etc/fstab"
cp -a /etc/fstab /etc/fstab.bak.$(date +%s)
if grep -qE '^\s*tmpfs\s+/dev/shm\s' /etc/fstab; then
  sudo -n sed -i -E 's#^\s*tmpfs\s+/dev/shm\s+tmpfs\s+.*#tmpfs /dev/shm tmpfs defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec,seclabel 0 0#' /etc/fstab
else
  echo 'tmpfs /dev/shm tmpfs defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec,seclabel 0 0' | sudo -n tee -a /etc/fstab
fi

echo "STEP 2: configure /tmp hardening via systemd tmp.mount drop-in"
sudo -n mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/tmp.mount.d
sudo -n tee /etc/systemd/system/tmp.mount.d/override.conf > /dev/null <<'EOF'
[Mount]
What=tmpfs
Type=tmpfs
Options=mode=1777,strictatime,nosuid,nodev,noexec
EOF

echo "STEP 3: reload systemd and apply"
sudo -n systemctl daemon-reload
sudo -n systemctl enable --now tmp.mount
sudo -n systemctl restart dev-shm.mount 2>/dev/null || sudo -n mount -o remount /dev/shm

echo "STEP 4: verify live mount options"
findmnt /tmp -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS
findmnt /dev/shm -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS

echo "STEP 5: verify enablement state (must survive reboot)"
systemctl is-enabled tmp.mount
grep -E '/dev/shm' /etc/fstab

echo "STEP 6: functional proof - exec and setuid/device denied"
set +e
echo '#!/bin/sh' > /tmp/exectest.sh
echo 'echo should-not-run' >> /tmp/exectest.sh
chmod +x /tmp/exectest.sh
/tmp/exectest.sh
echo "tmp_exec_rc=$?"

cp /bin/true /dev/shm/shmtest
chmod +x /dev/shm/shmtest
/dev/shm/shmtest
echo "shm_exec_rc=$?"

sudo -n touch /tmp/setuidtest
sudo -n chmod u+s /tmp/setuidtest
ls -l /tmp/setuidtest
stat -c '%A %a' /tmp/setuidtest
set -e
rm -f /tmp/exectest.sh /dev/shm/shmtest
sudo -n rm -f /tmp/setuidtest
echo "DONE"
